cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 'Then list the rivals' builds directly on T4's claim that lag needs a rival.
cells.limitation: T11 opens a new conflict without answering T10's revised test list.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 splits the feeling into envy, loneliness, clock; T6, T7 and section E use it.
cells.limitation: T10's test list is partly generic, adding little beyond T2's experiments.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T8 and T9 examine whether declining tests is independence or avoidance.
cells.limitation: Freedom versus closeness to friends surfaces only in T11 and is never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 narrows the Field Tester's experiments; T10 revises to 'pieces, not packages'.
cells.limitation: Imitation Detective's envy ranking is never reshaped by T8's guesswork objection.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates feeling behind from wanting the milestones, with three readings.
cells.limitation: Which reading is likeliest stays open with no sharper test than noticing spikes.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 restates its claim precisely: lag needs a rival, not that you want milestones.
cells.limitation: T8 casts Mill's view as never testing anything, stronger than T6 actually said.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 names independence as the assumption, calls untested oddness avoidance; T9 answers by narrowing.
cells.limitation: T7's challenge to loneliness rests on 'people often', an untested generalisation.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's 'experiments of living' matches Mill's On Liberty phrase; imitation paraphrase fits.
cells.limitation: T7's claim about how people mislabel ranking pain is unsupported; other attributions unverified.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A separates reported feeling from interpretation; T11 flags going beyond its source.
cells.limitation: T7 ranks envy over loneliness as a general fact without evidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 'Fair hit on one point'; T9 'Accepted'; T10 'Agreed, with a revision'.
cells.limitation: Imitation Detective never answers T8's charge that ranking motives is guesswork.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the decisive unknown: milestones, friendships, or a real deadline.
cells.limitation: T3's possibility that the user wants a different life is not pursued afterwards.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T9 ties tests to touring houses and dating; T10 asks married friends what to keep.
cells.limitation: Sparse input; T10's year of living arrangements is not drawn from any stated circumstance.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T11 'Which matters more is not mine to rank' keeps speaker values separate.
cells.limitation: The user's own positive priorities are never elicited beyond T10's chosen project.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T6: if a real deadline exists, drifting is a choice with a price.
cells.limitation: T10 calls a year of different living arrangements cheap, ignoring cost and reversibility.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on deadline, friend-specific spikes, neither, unknown, each with its implication.
cells.limitation: Deadline branch does not separate wanting children from a financial window.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 offers envy, loneliness, clock as alternatives; section D asks who the imagined audience is.
cells.limitation: T7 leans on 'people often' to rank envy above loneliness.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 'You both assume the doubt needs fixing'; T4 shows rebelling is also imitation.
cells.limitation: The assumption that friends' milestones left them better off is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T11 names that staying free and staying close to friends may pull apart.
cells.limitation: That value conflict arrives in the final turn and is never weighed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 and T7 name envy, loneliness, being ranked; T11 asks whose approval is imagined.
cells.limitation: Family or parental expectations, a common pressure source, are never raised.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T11 and section D leave the ranking and imagined-audience question to the user.
cells.limitation: T6 'let it ring unanswered' is Mill's verdict, not offered for the user to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lays out testing, repairing friendships, limiting comparison, and waiting.
cells.limitation: The decision itself is never stated; options appear only as branch outcomes.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T6: drifting has a price if a deadline exists; freedom is not costless.
cells.limitation: Section E says nothing is lost by waiting, despite T11's friendship tension.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: feeling spiking around particular friends or events favours repair over tests.
cells.limitation: T10's 'a year' and section E's 'a few weeks' are not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T6 'the clock is the missing fact' singles out the consequential unknown.
cells.limitation: Section D does not rank remaining unknowns once the clock question is settled.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: notice when the feeling spikes; ask friends what they would keep and drop.
cells.limitation: T10's year of different living arrangements is out of proportion to an unsure feeling.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: Plain images like 'scoreboard' and 'pieces, not packages' carry the theories without jargon.
cells.limitation: T2 'their head' and T3, T9 'this person' slip into third person about the user.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 addresses Mill by name; T9 'Accepted' clearly answers T8.
cells.limitation: T4 'Fair hit on one point' does not say which T3 point.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within 25 to 65 words, with varied length.
cells.limitation: T11 opens a new conflict too late to be developed.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Field Tester's bluntness in T8 contrasts with Mill's principled narrowing in T9.
cells.limitation: All three lean on 'I would'; Detective and Mill share a similar register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; T5 and T6 move straight to new content.
cells.limitation: Section E partly repeats section D's three readings.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T6 and T11 put real costs on the table: a clock and drifting friendships.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete scene from the user's friendships appears.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 Mill accepts T8's hiding-place charge, narrowing tests: 'custom wearing a lab coat'.
cells.limitation: Shifts are narrowings, not reversals; no mind changes its core position.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T8 'avoidance with good branding' gives the Field Tester a distinct blunt edge.
cells.limitation: Mill's voice is modern and plain, with little distinct character.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: 'Custom wearing a lab coat' (T9) and 'avoidance with good branding' (T8) land sharply.
cells.limitation: Imitation Detective's later turns T7 and T11 are plainer than its T1 opener.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: Tension builds to T8's challenge of Mill, then resolves into T9 and T10 revisions.
cells.limitation: T11 ends on a new conflict rather than an emotional landing.

strengths: Field Tester's T5 split into envy, loneliness and a real clock drives T6, T7 and section E.
T8 to T10: the hiding-place charge makes Mill narrow tests and the Field Tester revise to pieces.
Section E turns missing facts into observable branches, each naming the option it favours.
weaknesses: Imitation Detective's T11 freedom-versus-closeness conflict arrives last and is never weighed.
Section E treats waiting as costless in the no-deadline branch despite drifting friendships.
Field Tester's T10 'a year of different living arrangements' is called cheap but is ungrounded and disproportionate.

symptoms.observed: Core value conflict named only in the final turn, never weighed by any mind.
symptoms.evidence: staying free and staying close to friends may pull apart

symptoms.observed: A year-long living change offered as a cheap, reversible test; number not from user facts.
symptoms.evidence: Try a year of different living arrangements.

symptoms.observed: Envy ranked above loneliness via an unsupported generalisation about people.
symptoms.evidence: People often call it missing friends when the sharper pain is being ranked

symptoms.observed: Imitation Detective never answers T8's guesswork charge; shifts to a new topic instead.
symptoms.evidence: Blunt version: ranking motives from here is guesswork.

symptoms.observed: Concession does not specify which point of T3 it accepts.

findings.description: Generalisation that people mislabel the pain of being ranked as missing friends is asserted without support and used to rank motives.
Attributions to Girard, Ibarra and Mill cannot be checked here; T3's 'experiments of living' is consistent with recall of On Liberty.

rubric_fit_notes: The user's input is two sentences, so C3.2 and C3.4 were judged against how well the sparse context was used. Section E's 'a few weeks' is a minor ungrounded number outside the turns.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (self_reflection): the choice is how to respond to feeling behind, so waiting, learning more and limited tests count as options.
